topics.title: RBI raised the repo rate: what it really does to your home loan EMI
topics.angle: When the hike reaches your loan, how much it costs over the full term, and the two ways to absorb it (bigger EMI or longer tenure)
topics.why_now: MPC raised repo 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, the first hike since Feb 2023, and moved to 'calibrated tightening'. Floating-rate borrowers will see it at their next reset; repo/EMI videos are among this week's fastest-growing long videos in the niche (Sagar Sinha, Mumbai Tak). For 25-40 salaried borrowers.
outline: hook: Rohan's bank SMS: 'your loan rate is revised'. The extra interest over the remaining term, as one number
chapter 1, what happened: repo up a quarter point; what the repo rate is, in one picture (a tap upstream of every bank)
how it reaches a floating loan: the external benchmark, the bank's spread, the reset date (Sharma has lived through 2022-23)
the setup: a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan at 8.50% vs 8.75%
split: old EMI vs new EMI, the monthly difference looks small
reveal: the same difference over 240 months, total interest side by side
chapter 2, the trap: banks often stretch the tenure instead of raising the EMI; calendar flipping the extra months
towers: total interest if the EMI rises vs if the tenure stretches
Priya: why the 'free' option is the expensive one
chapter 3, the other side: savers; an FD at a higher rate, lumpsum over five years
what to do: check your reset date, ask the bank which option they applied, choose EMI over tenure if the budget allows
checklist recap, three steps
end
topics.maths: two emi (same amount and months, 8.50% vs 8.75%) for the EMI rise and total interest; a third emi with the higher rate at a longer months count is NOT computable yet (tenure needs solving) - either show only the EMI-rise path, or wait for the loan_prepay/tenure kind (backlog 2026-10-18-maths-loan-tenure); two lumpsum for the FD side
topics.facts_hint: repo 5.25% -> 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026; confirm on the RBI monetary policy statement at rbi.org.in before using as a sourced fact
verify: Repo rate 5.50% from 5.25% on 7 Oct 2026, on rbi.org.in
That repo-linked (EBLR) home loans reset at least every three months per RBI rules
Typical home loan rates near 8.5% at the time of writing
That banks may extend tenure rather than raise EMI on a rate rise, and RBI's 2023 rule letting borrowers choose

topics.title: Prepaying your home loan: cut the EMI or cut the years?
topics.angle: With a bonus in hand, which prepayment choice saves more, by how much, and when the 'worse' one is still right
topics.why_now: A decision every home-loan holder faces at bonus time, searched all year ('reduce EMI or tenure'); more pressing now that rates are rising. Fintech and lender blogs answer it with tables; nobody shows it as a story.
outline: hook: Rohan gets a ₹3 lakh bonus. Two buttons on the bank's app; one saves lakhs more
chapter 1, the loan: ₹40 lakh, 20 years; why the first years are mostly interest (the interest monster eating the early EMIs)
choice A, cut the EMI: same years, smaller EMI, interest saved
choice B, cut the years: same EMI, the calendar stops early; interest saved
towers: A vs B interest saved, the reveal
Sharma: 'I prepaid in year fifteen once. It barely mattered' - timing chart, the same prepayment in year 2 vs year 12
chapter 2, when A is right: a tight budget, or investing the freed EMI (a sip at 12% vs the loan rate)
split: B's interest saved vs A plus the freed EMI invested
the catch: fixed-rate loans can charge prepayment fees; floating ones for individuals generally cannot
checklist: what to ask the bank before you prepay
recap
end
topics.maths: emi for the base loan and for the reduced-EMI case (smaller amount, same months); the reduced-tenure months and interest need a new loan_prepay kind (backlog 2026-10-18-maths-loan-tenure); one sip for the invested freed EMI. Not usable until that kind exists unless Studio tells only choice A plus the sip.
verify: RBI rule that individual floating-rate home loans carry no prepayment charges

topics.title: Your salary went up. Why do you still feel broke?
topics.angle: How spending that rises with every raise (plus inflation) eats the raise, and what saving half of each hike is worth over 15 years
topics.why_now: 'Why a normal life now feels like a luxury' was the fastest-growing long video in our niche this week (~13.6k views/hour); the feeling is universal for 25-35 salaried viewers and fully computable.
outline: hook: Rohan's salary doubled in eight years. His savings didn't move. The one number that explains it
chapter 1, the treadmill (the one picture): every raise speeds up the treadmill, he stays in place
what ₹40,000 of monthly expenses costs in 10 and 15 years at 6% inflation (bignumber)
Rohan upgrades: the flat, the car EMI, the deliveries; each raise spent the month it lands
Priya's rule: half of every raise goes to a SIP before it hits the account
chapter 2, a year of it: the first hike invested, small
chart: Priya's SIP pot over 15 years vs Rohan's zero
reveal: the gap at year 15
Sharma: 'the raise is real, the extra lifestyle is a loan from your future self'
chapter 3, what to do: automate the split on appraisal day; checklist
recap
end
topics.maths: a lumpsum at the inflation rate for future expenses (₹40,000 at 6% over 10 and 15 years); a sip for the invested half-raise (e.g. ₹5,000 at 11% for 15 years; a true yearly step-up needs the sip_stepup kind, backlog 2026-10-18-maths-sip-stepup, so tell it as one invested hike until then)

That 11% equity return is stated as an assumption

topics.why_now: A warikoo video on exactly this pain is growing fast this week (~3.9k views/hour). Most of our audience starts here; we take the subject, not the treatment: our version is the numbers.

the first ₹1,000: an emergency buffer before investing (calendar flipping the months to three months of expenses)
chapter 2, the small SIP: ₹2,000 a month at 11% for 20 years (snowball)
reveal: final vs invested, the ratio
Sharma: 'I started with ₹500. Starting mattered more than the amount'
split: start now with ₹2,000 vs wait five years and start with ₹4,000
the traps at this salary: buy-now-pay-later, card minimum due (quick card_min_due beat)
chapter 3, when the salary grows: raise the SIP with it
checklist: three things for this month
recap
end
